sentences.text: This appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) has been filed by the claim petitioner in O.P.(MV) No.1119 of 2018 on the file of the Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Ernakulam, (the Tribunal), aggrieved by the amount of compensation granted by Award dated 22/02/2020.

entities.text: Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Ernakulam
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The sole respondent herein is the 3rd respondent/insurer in the petition.
In this appeal, the parties and the documents will be referred to as described in the original petition.

2. According to the claim petitioner, on 06/03/2018 at about 04:00 p.m., while he was standing in the autorickshaw stand at Nadakkavu junction, car bearing registration no.KL-5-AF-5285 driven by the first respondent in a rash and negligent manner, knocked him down, as a result of which he sustained grievous injuries.
3. The first respondent/driver and the second respondent/owner filed written statement denying negligence on the part of the former.
4. The third respondent/insurer filed written statement admitting the policy but denying negligence on the part of the first respondent/driver of the offending car.
The age, occupation and income were disputed.
5. Before the Tribunal, no oral evidence was adduced by either side.
Exts. A1
to A5 were marked on the side of the claim petitioner.
No documentary evidence was produced by the respondents.
Ext.X1 disability certificate was also marked.

6. The Tribunal on consideration of the documentary evidence and after hearing both sides, found negligence on the part of the first respondent/driver of the offending car resulting in the incident and hence awarded an amount of 5,11,836/- together with interest @ 8% per annum from the date Ratheesh C.R vs The Divisional Manager on 26 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189966637/
2 of petition till realisation along with proportionate costs.

entities.text: Ratheesh C.R vs The Divisional Manager
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Aggrieved by the Award, the claim petitioner has come up in appeal.
The only point that arises for consideration in this appeal is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.
8. Heard both sides.
9. The award of compensation by the Tribunal under the following heads is challenged by the claim petitioner- Loss of earnings
The materials on record show that the claim petitioner sustained the following injuries- 1. Lacerated wound 3x2cm upper left arm.

2. Laceration on the tip of the right nostril.
3. Lacerated wound right side of face near eye.
4. Poly trauma-Grade IV splenic injury left 3-7 rib fracture.
5.
Left ulnar fracture.
He was hospitalised for a period of 7 days.
In all probability, he might have been unable to work for a period of 8 months.

Therefore, he can be awarded compensation for a period of 8 months, that is,
11,500/-x8 months = 92,000/-.
Compensation for loss of amenities and enjoyment in life 10.
An amount of 1,50,000/- was claimed.
The Tribunal 2025:KER:72513 granted an amount of 35,000/-.
In the facts and circumstances of the case, an amount of 55,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.
11. I.A.No.1 of 2021 has been filed for receiving additional documents to show the expenses incurred towards treatment of the claim petitioner.

The application is opposed by the learned counsel for third respondent/insurer, who points out that a perusal of the bills would show that the treatment and the medicines taken has got nothing to do with the injuries sustained by the claim petitioner and therefore, the same cannot be taken into consideration.
11.1. A perusal of the bills shows that it was for treatment of dengue and routine tests seen conducted for diabetes and other connected tests.
Most of the medicines seem to be relating to diabetes, which also has no connection with the injuries sustained by the claim petitioner.

That being the position, this Court is unable to accept the argument of the learned counsel for the claim Ratheesh C.R vs The Divisional Manager on 26 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189966637/
3 petitioner that the expenses incurred, as evident from the said bills, were incurred due to treatment for the injuries sustained.

sentences.text: Hence, I.A.No.1/2021 is dismissed.

12. The impugned Award is modified to the following 2025:KER:72513 extent :
Sl. Head of claim Amount Amount Modified in No. claimed Awarded by appeal Tribunal 1 Loss of earning 2,00,000/- 69,000/- 92,000/-
(11,500/-x 8 months) 2 Transport to 5,000/- 10,000/- 10,000/-
 hospital (No modification)
 3 Extra 20,000/- 15,000/- 15,000/-
 nourishment (No modification)
 4 Damage to 5,000/- 2,000/- 2,000/-
 clothing (No modification)
 5 Treatment 4,00,000/- 2,89,536/- 2,89,536/-
 expenses (No modification)
6 Bystanders
expenses (No modification)

7 Compensation 2,50,000/- 65,000/- 65,000/-
 for pain and (No modification)
 sufferings  8 Compensation 1,50,000/- 35,000/- 55,000/-
 for loss of  amenities &
 enjoyment in life
9 Compensation
for disability

10 Compensation 50,000/- -- --
 for disfiguration (No modification)
 11 Future treatment 50,000/- -- --
 expenses (No modification)
 Total 16,50,000/- 5,11,836/- 5,54,836/-
In the result, the appeal is allowed by enhancing the compensation by a further amount of 43,000/- (total compensation 2025:KER:72513 =5,54,836/- that is, 5,11,836/- granted by the Tribunal + 43,000/- granted in appeal) with interest at the rate of 8% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization (excluding the period of 89 days delay in filing the appeal) and proportionate costs.
The third respondent/insurer is directed to deposit the compensation with interest and costs before the Tribunal within a period of 60 days from the date of receipt of a copy of the judgment.
On deposit of the compensation amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the amount to the claim petitioner at the earliest in accordance with law after making deductions, if any.
Interlocutory applications, if any pending, shall stand closed.
